line: So icy my whole career (It’s Gucci)
vault_lines: So icy my whole career (It's Gucci)
meaning:
“Icy” is one of Gucci Mane’s early success, a famous single produced by Gucci’s frequent collaborator Zaytoven released in 2005. On the song, Guwop raps:

All these girls excited
Ooh, you know they like it
I’m so icy, so icy

More recently, the Atlanta rapper dropped his 12th studio album titled El Gato: The Human Glacier and was featured on Logic’s song “Icy”, on which he raps:

I’m a human glacier, wrist full of frozen water (Well, damn)

To be icy means be rich, and more precisely to own a lot of jewelry, which is often depicted in hip hop by the motif of ice. Gucci embodies the ice in the most concrete way via the ice cream tattoo on his cheek.



Gucci also said he’d consider his way of life “icy” in an interview on Rolling Stone.

line: Richard Mille cost me a ’rari (And what?)
vault_lines: Richard Mille cost me a 'rari (And what?)
meaning:
Richard Mille is a Swiss luxury watch brand founded by Richard Mille and Dominique Guenat in 2001. These luxury watches can cost as little as $70,000 to the $2.5 million sapphire timepiece that Jay Z bought back in April of 2019.

A “‘rari” refers to the luxury Italian sport car manufacturer, Ferrari, that was founded in 1947 by Enzo Ferrari. These automobiles, when purchased new, can range from $200,000 to $350,000.

21 Savage compares the cost of his Richard Mille watch to the cost of a Ferrari luxury sports car.



21 Savage at the Versace Pre-Fall 2019 show in 2018 wearing Versace clothes and a Richard Mille watch


This isn’t the first time 21 has rapped about Richard Mille watches as he has already done so on the songs “Floating,” “asmr,” “Wish Wish” and “Legacy”. Savage previously mentioned Ferrari’s on the songs “Bank Account,” “Rap Saved Me,” “monster” and more.

line: Got a couple hits, but he ain’t right though (You cappin’)
vault_lines: Got a couple hits, but he ain't right though (You cappin')
meaning:
This line was first transcribed on here as “but he ain’t write though,” but the correct word is more likely the homonym, “right.” Michael Jackson is recognized as not only a performer but also a songwriter. 21’s not likely denying that fact, but nonchalantly downplays MJ’s success with “got a couple hits” (MJ actually had 31 songs enter the Billboard Top 10), specifically because “he ain’t right”—referencing sexual abuse accusations against MJ going back to at least the 1990s and recently underscored by the documentary Leaving Neverland.

21’s not the only one grappling with the so-called King of Pop’s questionable legacy. Gucci Mane makes a similar suggestion on Lil Baby’s Realist in It, with the line “Michael Jackson with the glove, Annie, are you okay? (Wow)” The whole verse is about Guwop being a badass, and in this line associating himself with MJ “with the glove” infers criminal intent, like maybe Annie is not, in fact, okay, but is in his clutches. In a culture where MJ is still enshrined despite repeated accusations and revelations, Gucci’s scandalous claiming of MJ as sick, if smooth, criminal startles even him—“wow.” 21’s verse getting capped off with “You cappin” implies he’s out for character assassination in a more determined fashion.

line: Suicidal doors got me flier than a bird (Flier)
vault_lines: Suicidal doors got me flier than a bird (Flier)
meaning:
Made popular by models like the early Lincoln Continental and Ford Thunderbird, suicide doors open opposite the way normal vehicle doors open.

Dave Brownell, former editor of Hemmings Motor News, said this on the suicide doors:

Suicide doors were especially popular with mobsters in the gangster era of the 1930s, supposedly owing to the ease of pushing passengers out of moving vehicles.

Recently though, luxury brand Rolls-Royce has been incorporating suicide doors into their newer models which is most likely what Offset is mentioning here.

line: Panamera 911 off-white verge (Off-white)

The Porsche Panamera is Porsche’s full-size luxury sedan. They started production in 2009 and have gone through various generations and styles. With some of the higher end models starting at 160k. They reference one that is “off-white” simultaneously stating what physical color it is and name dropping the popular fashion brand. (off-white is typically a beige/pearly neutral color).



Also, “verge” is probably a play on the name of Off-White’s owner, Virgil Abloh, because it sounds like “Virg”

Why you got a 12 car garage? (Why?)

line: But I got a whole lotta M’s though (Racks) Bitch, you wasn’t with me shootin’ in the gym ho (No cap)
vault_lines: But I got a whole lotta M's though (Racks)
meaning:
On “Stay Schemin,” both Drake and Rick Ross rapped:

Bitch, you wasn’t with me shootin' in the gym
(huh! Bitch, you wasn’t with me shootin' in the gym)

The lines are a reference to NBA great Kobe Bryant’s wife Vanessa Bryant, who had filed for divorce from him in 2011. Had they gone through with the divorce, Vanessa would’ve profited handsomely, even though she hadn’t actually put in the same effort as Kobe had when it came to amassing the fortune.

In other words, if you weren’t there while he was grinding, you shouldn’t expect to profit off 21’s newfound wealth either.

line: Shinin’ like the glove on Michael (Jackson)
vault_lines: Shinin' like the glove on Michael (Jackson)
meaning:
21 mentions Michael Jackson’s iconic glove, which was encrusted with was a trademark possession of his. The sequined glove was worth over $60,000 and was reportedly used to conceal his vitiligo, although that is unconfirmed.

21 Savage compares his level of fame and recognition to the “shine” that the diamonds on Jackson’s glove reflects.

line: I ain’t really sendin’ no hearts though (On God)
vault_lines: I ain't really sendin' no hearts though (On God)
meaning:
21 cleverly references his 2016 track, “No Heart.” On the chorus, he rapped:

‘Cause these niggas pussy and I’m hard
I turn that fuckin’ soft into some hard
I grew up in the streets without no heart

21 is sending a girl a direct message, continuing the scenario he began describing in the previous line. He refuses to tell the girl he loves her (hearts are utilized as emojis that indicate love) and claims that he is only engaged in the conversation for the sexual benefits.

This could also reference Drake’s refrain on 2017 track “Sneakin',” which 21 featured on. On the track, he said:

FaceTime with my shawty on tour
And she textin' purple hearts ‘cause she know that we at war, yuh

line: Got that Roll’ and it’s snatchin’, I keep more snow than Aspen
vault_lines: Got that Roll' and it's snatchin', I keep more snow than Aspen
meaning:
Future is stacking two flexes in one bar.

“Got that Rollie and it’s snatchin’” means his Rolex is eye-catching — it “snatches” attention the moment people see it. The watch represents status and wealth.

“I keep more snow than Aspen” uses a double meaning. “Snow” is slang for cocaine, while Aspen is famous for heavy snowfall. He’s saying he has a massive supply, while also reinforcing how rich and excessive his lifestyle is.

Overall, the line is about luxury and abundance, using visual imagery to exaggerate how far ahead he has come.

line: Shots and contusions, the gas bad for pollution (Woah, woah, woah, let’s go)
vault_lines: Shots and contusions, the gas bad for pollution (Woah, woah, woah, let's go)
meaning: “Shots and contusions” suggests physical violence and injury—“shots” like gunfire and “contusions” as bruises from impact—while “the gas bad for pollution” shifts the focus to environmental harm, hinting at potent emissions from burning gasoline (petrol),  however, Travis is not a climate activist, he instead using “gas” as slang term for potent weed, Travis is referencing that he is smoking so much of said “gas” that it could cause severere local pollution.

line: As-salamu alayk’, I’m with DJ Snake
vault_lines: As-salamu alayk', I'm with DJ Snake
meaning:
“Assalamu alaikum” is one of the greeting form in Arabic meaning “Peace be upon you.”

From the start, Future gives a nod of respect to DJ Snake’s cultural background. DJ Snake is a French-born producer of Algerian descent. Algeria is a North African country with Arabic being one of its main languages.

line: I’m tsunami like Wheez’, I’ma trap it, yeah, yeah (Yeah, woo)
vault_lines: I'm tsunami like Wheez', I'ma trap it, yeah, yeah (Yeah, woo)
meaning:
Travis shouts out Atlanta-native Wheezy, one of the most successful modern trap producers. He worked with Travis on tracks like “MY EYES”, “TOPIA TWINS”, “Best Man”, and many others.

Aside from his iconic “Wheezy outta here” tag, he also has less-known producer tags like “Tsunami” and “The tsunami warning has been issued” coming from his nickname Young Wheezy the Wave.

Additionally, Travis plays it off with homophones “wave” and “waive” in his verse.
